records.recommendation: Consider a planned retirement entry for GT A and a note for GT E and GT B and C
records.researcher_notes: The 2025 decision text says gas turbine A is to be shut down at the latest when the new gas plant is reliably in operation. Gas turbine E is to move into the grid reserve. Gas turbines B and C are to stay in service. The text gives no year, so no planned retirement year can be set. This was outside the checks for this follow-up.

records.recommendation: Keep the capacity question open
records.researcher_notes: The permits state only thermal input of up to 1,140 MW. No electric figure appears in the published decisions.

records.recommendation: Check whether Iqony GmbH is the same company as STEAG GmbH, the owner GEM lists, before changing the owner.
records.researcher_notes: The application of 17 July 2025 for a preliminary decision was filed by Iqony GmbH, Rüttenscheider Straße 1-3, Essen. GEM lists STEAG GmbH as owner. My search of the entity records found no entry named Iqony GmbH. I did not change the owner because an application is not a completed ownership change.

records.recommendation: Keep 880 MW. The notice gives a thermal input of 1,392 MW under standard conditions, which is not electric capacity.
records.researcher_notes: The notice describes the plant as ready for hydrogen, with up to 4,000 operating hours a year. It gives no electric output in MW.

records.recommendation: No change. The register page lists the application with public display from 13 October to 12 November 2025 and no decision date.
records.researcher_notes: No preliminary decision or permit was found in the register page. A separate water discharge application to the Lippe river was filed on the same date. The page of the Arnsberg district government itself refused the fetcher, so its text was confirmed from a saved copy.

records.recommendation: Keep pre-construction. Note the first partial building permit of 14 April 2025 in the status detail if wanted.
records.researcher_notes: The register page for the EVC 3 procedure gives 14 April 2025 as the decision date for the first partial permit. The Saxony official gazette issue 25 of 2025 lists the public notice dated 21 May 2025. The notice itself could not be opened because the register refused requests, so no capacity or start date was read from it.

records.recommendation: Keep 39.0 MW until the engine replacement is confirmed. After it, the permit documents give 47.5 MW electric for this block.
records.researcher_notes: The first partial permit of 20 December 2023 and the 2022 environmental report say the nine existing engines of 3.88 MW each, about 34.9 MW in total, are replaced by nine engines of 5.28 MW each, 47.5 MW in total, between 2024 and 2026. The 2023 notice gave January 2024 as the planned start. I found no report that the work is finished.

records.recommendation: Keep as is. The permit file says EVC 1 gets the same engine replacement, from about 34.9 MW to 47.5 MW.
records.researcher_notes: The 2022 environmental report describes the EVC 1 work in the same way as EVC 2. The permit for EVC 1 is a separate procedure that was not in the collected files.

records.recommendation: Keep MTU 4000 Series for now. The environmental report names a different make as expected.
records.researcher_notes: The report names Bergen Engines type B36:45 L9AG1 as the expected maker for the replacement engines of EVC 1 and says the same engines are used in all three blocks. It says expected, not ordered. GEM lists MTU 4000 Series. The saved Wayback copy was used to check the report text.

records.recommendation: Check the company name. GEM lists Energieversorgungscenter Dresden-Wilschdorf GmbH & Co KG.
records.researcher_notes: The permit files name Zweite Energieversorgungscenter Dresden-Wilschdorf GmbH & Co. KG as applicant. The register title for the EVC 3 permit names GlobalFoundries Dresden Module One LLC & Co. KG. Neither name was found in the entity records, so I did not change the owner.

records.recommendation: No action. The register file collected for this plant is for a different RWE project.
records.researcher_notes: The saved register summary describes an RWE gas engine plant at Knapsacker Hügel in Hürth, with 278 MW and a decision dated 2 September 2026. That is not Gundremmingen, so it was not used. The Swabia district government notice and permit file were used instead.

records.recommendation: Keep pre-construction. Look for the permit decision in the Swabia district government pages later.
records.researcher_notes: The application was filed in December 2024 and publicly noticed on 4 March 2025. The Swabia district government page for the project, read on 6 October 2026, shows the application for up to 124 MW of electric output and the public display from 11 March to 10 April 2025. It shows no decision yet. No start of construction was found.

records.recommendation: Check that the permitted site matches this GEM plant.
records.researcher_notes: The register entry places the storage power plant at Neuendorf in the municipality of Teichland, while GEM places the unit at Peitz. The project name matches the LEAG storage power plant at Jänschwalde, but I did not find a document that names both places together.

records.recommendation: Decide whether the data center use makes this a captive plant.
records.researcher_notes: KMW says the main job of the plant is emergency power for the Green Rocks data center, and that it also feeds the grid about 2,000 hours a year. I left the captive fields alone.

records.recommendation: Check what the 550 MW for the second unit is based on. Consider whether the second unit is the second block of the 2018 permit, which is 319 MW net.
records.researcher_notes: The Regierung von Schwaben decision of 4 December 2018 approves two gas turbine blocks. It states the plant as about 638 MW net, which is 2 x 319 MW at 15 degrees Celsius, and up to about 674 MW, which is 2 x 337 MW. Only one block is listed in GEM as built, at 319 MW. The 550 MW for the second unit may come from a later and different plan. The owner's page mentions a new second plant by 2030. I did not change the value.

records.recommendation: Confirm how the permit holder relates to the owner in GEM.
records.researcher_notes: The permit was issued to Gaskraftwerk Leipheim GmbH & Co. KG in Ulm. GEM lists Lausitz Energie Kraftwerke AG at 100 percent. The permit does not say who owns the company. I did not change the owner.

records.recommendation: The 2018 permit alone does not support construction. The earlier question about announced versus pre-construction still stands.
records.researcher_notes: The state planning decision for the gas pipeline dated 28 June 2019 and the 2018 plant permit are both old. I found no newer official notice for a second block.

records.recommendation: Consider adding the 12 March 2024 permit decision to the notes for this unit.
records.researcher_notes: The register entry confirms a granted permit for the hydrogen gas turbine on 12 March 2024. The permit text itself was not in the saved files, so the capacity and fuel mix are not confirmed from it.

records.recommendation: Check where the 2040 planned retirement comes from.
records.researcher_notes: A local land use plan document dated April 2026 says the Lippendorf coal plant will close for good on 31 December 2035. That is a different unit. Nothing in these documents gives a closure date for the gas plant.

records.recommendation: No change. The permit notice gives a thermal input of up to 1,417 MW but no electric capacity and no start date. Look for these in later permits.
records.researcher_notes: The register page for this procedure shows no details, but the permit notice was read on the Neukieritzsch town website, which posts the same notice. It covers only the gatehouse, construction roads, gas turbine foundation and site office. It gives a thermal input of up to 1,417 MW. It does not give an electric capacity or a planned start date. A search summary mentioned a start in the second quarter of 2027, but that wording matches the Schwarze Pumpe notice, so I did not use it.

records.recommendation: No change. Noted for the reviewer.
records.researcher_notes: The permit register page for the two new gas turbines at the West plant shows only the 2022 public display of the application. It does not show the permit decisions, which would be in partial permits not listed there. The owner's June 2026 press release remains the best dated source for the project.

records.recommendation: Check whether the preliminary decision is still valid.
records.researcher_notes: The decision says it lapses unless the company applies for a first partial permit or full permit within 2 years after the decision becomes final. That period can be extended to 4 years on request. The decision is dated 29 May 2024, so the first deadline may already be near or past. I found no application for a permit and no sign the company has asked for an extension.

records.recommendation: Keep 50 MW as a placeholder and look for the electric output in the engine supplier documents.
records.researcher_notes: The permit notice states no electric output. The earlier research found the 12 modules have about 125 MW of fuel input in total, which is thermal input, not capacity. The 50 MW in the database is not confirmed by any document read.

records.recommendation: Check whether the industrial gas turbine plant should be a separate unit or added to the capacity.
records.researcher_notes: The application covers a combined cycle plant, a standby power plant and an industrial gas turbine plant at the same site. GEM has one unit of 900 MW. The first partial permit of 18 March 2026 gives the thermal input of each part: up to 1,590 MW for the single shaft combined cycle plant, up to 68 MW for the standby plant, and up to 246 MW for the gas turbine plant with two small turbines, or 222 MW with one. It gives no electric output for any part, and the turbine design is not yet chosen.

records.recommendation: Leave the coordinates as they are. The environmental impact report should be read when the register allows it.
records.researcher_notes: The notices name the parcels in the district Korbetha, not coordinates. No document read states a latitude or longitude, so the coordinates stay unconfirmed.

records.recommendation: Keep 850 MW from LEAG's 2025 release unless a later permit shows otherwise.
records.researcher_notes: The decision of 14 October 2024 states a gross electric output of 875 MW and a net output of 855 MW. Thermal fuel input is 1,417 MW and is not capacity. GEM has 850 MW from a LEAG release of August 2025. The permit figure is from the older design, so the two differ.

records.recommendation: Leave the start year at 2028 for now.
records.researcher_notes: The 2022 application and the October 2024 decision both say commissioning was planned for the second quarter of 2027. That date is old and no second partial permit has been published. The earlier research found no newer official date.

records.recommendation: Reconsider the earlier batch's move from announced to pre-construction for block 8.
records.researcher_notes: The permit file is only a preliminary decision. Under the lifecycle rules a preliminary decision supports pre-construction only together with the operator's final investment decision. I found no Uniper investment decision, and the project still depends on the capacity tender award due by 3 November 2026. So announced is the safer status for now.

records.recommendation: Do not fill Latest Activity for block 8.
records.researcher_notes: The earlier batch proposed 18 August 2026 from a trade press article. That report is within the last twelve months and the project is moving, so the rule says to leave this field blank. The preliminary decision itself is dated 18 February 2026, not April 2026. The April 2026 date was the date of the news reports.

records.recommendation: Check whether the owner for block 8 should be Uniper Kraftwerke GmbH instead of Uniper SE.
records.researcher_notes: The permit applicant and holder is Uniper Kraftwerke GmbH, which is also the owner GEM lists for block 4. GEM lists Uniper SE for block 8. A permit applicant is not proof of ownership and an owner change needs a closed transaction, so I did not report a change. The existing entity for Uniper covers this company name.

records.recommendation: No action. The saved permit register summary for this plant is for a different project.
records.researcher_notes: The summary file for this plant lists a heating plant application in Herne. It does not concern Staudinger block 8, so I did not use it.

records.recommendation: Check whether the owner should be RWE Generation SE instead of RWE AG.
records.researcher_notes: The permit applicant is RWE Generation SE. GEM lists RWE AG. An applicant is not proof of ownership and an owner change needs a closed transaction, so I did not report a change.

records.recommendation: Reconsider the earlier batch's move to pre-construction.
records.researcher_notes: A permit application supports announced at least. Pre-construction also needs a final investment decision. RWE says it will not build without a tender award, which is due by 3 November 2026. So announced may be the safer status for now.

records.recommendation: Do not fill Latest Activity for Voerde.
records.researcher_notes: The earlier batch proposed 28 July 2026. That is within the last twelve months and the project is moving, so the rule says to leave it blank.

records.recommendation: No action. The saved permit register summary for this plant is for a different project.
records.researcher_notes: The summary file lists a Herdecke engine plant application, not Voerde, so I did not use it.

records.recommendation: Review the owner of the new gas unit. The permit applicant was Hamburger Energiewerke GmbH, not Vattenfall.
records.researcher_notes: The Hamburg environment authority notice says the full permit of 24 August 2022 for the Dradenau gas and steam turbine plant went to Hamburger Energiewerke GmbH, formerly Wärme Hamburg GmbH. GEM shows Vattenfall Europe Power Management GmbH at 100 percent. I did not change the owner because the rules ask for a closed transaction from two publishers, and a permit applicant is not the same as a recorded owner. The earlier batch raised the same question for the coal blocks.

records.recommendation: Consider changing the owner to RWE Generation SE when a second independent source confirms who holds the plant.
records.researcher_notes: The permit of September 2026, the public notice of August 2025 and the official gazette of 2025 all name RWE Generation SE as the applicant. GEM shows RWE Power AG at 100 percent. The entity lookup finds RWE Generation SE as an existing owner on 144 units. I did not change the owner because the rules need a closed transaction or two independent publishers, and all these notices come from one authority.

records.recommendation: Check the procedure page of the permit register once it loads.
records.researcher_notes: The environmental register page for this plant lists a decision date of 7 September 2026. Its two documents did not load in time, so I read the official gazette notice of the same decision instead.

records.recommendation: Check whether the owner should be Onyx Waermekraftwerk Zolling GmbH instead of Onyx Germany GmbH.
records.researcher_notes: The public notice of January 2023 names Onyx Waermekraftwerk Zolling GmbH as the company that applied for the engine plant. GEM shows Onyx Germany GmbH at 100 percent. The entity lookup finds Onyx Germany but not the Zolling company. I did not change the owner because an applicant is not proof of who holds the plant.

records.recommendation: Check the capacity of 105 MW against the permit and the plant owner's figures.
records.researcher_notes: The 2020 permit states a net electric output of about 100 MW. The earlier batch found reports of 104 MW in total. GEM records 105 MW from 3 engines of 35 MW each. The permit describes up to 10 gas engines, and the earlier batch found nine engines. The engine count and the per-engine figure in GEM look wrong. I did not change them because the permit gives a plan and not the built plant.

records.recommendation: Check the owner of both units. GEM lists Zweckverband Müllverwertungsanlage Ingolstadt.
records.researcher_notes: The Uniper List of Assets for the year 2025 lists Ingolstadt 3 and 4 as fully consolidated Uniper assets at 100 percent. An Upper Bavaria district government order of 2 July 2024 is addressed to Uniper Kraftwerke GmbH as the operator of Units 3 and 4. The earlier batch raised the same question. The start year in the list is 1973 for Unit 3 and GEM has 1974. The year is a small gap and I did not change it.

records.recommendation: Consider renaming the unit and correcting the technology to internal combustion with two engines.
